report.summary: Chunk 5 of 7: implements docref resolution logic for path-based, dotted, and module-relative references; includes fallback to class member lookup and handling of absent submodules.
risks: line 555 | medium | Fallback to class member lookup is deliberately loose; may resolve symbols that are not actually meant (e.g., method with same name in different class). Additional context would settle if this causes false negatives.
line 482 | low | Uses _by_path which is defined outside this chunk; its behavior is uncheckable. Verification of _by_path implementation would settle.
line 512 | low | _module_file is used but defined elsewhere; its resolution logic is uncheckable. Verification of _module_file would settle.
line 519 | medium | anchored flag is set based on _module_file with suffixes=None; the semantics of this call are unclear without seeing _module_file. Review of _module_file signature would settle.

handoff.purpose: Resolve doc references to module paths and symbols, handling various reference formats and fallback to class members.

symbols.name: module
symbols.note: Local variable to store resolved module Path; initialized to None.

symbols.name: chain
symbols.note: Tuple of remaining symbol parts after module resolution; initialized to ().

symbols.name: anchored
symbols.note: Boolean flag indicating if the reference is anchored to a real module path; initialized to False.

symbols.name: _rel_key
symbols.note: Normalises a repo-relative path to a string using forward slashes.

claims.text: `path/to/mod.py::symbol` is a COMMITMENT by the author: a .py file and a name inside it. No competing reading exists, so a failure here is a finding rather than a guess about what they meant.
claims.why: The code at lines 483-486 matches this pattern and returns module, chain, anchored = candidate, (m.group(2),), True. If candidate is None, it falls through; otherwise it sets anchored=True, which treats failure as a finding.

claims.text: LONGEST module prefix wins: `daedalus.spine.picker.build_queue` must resolve to the module picker.py, not stop at the package daedalus.
claims.why: The loop at lines 514-519 iterates from len(parts) down to 1, checking each prefix; the first match (longest) is used, as seen in the break after assignment.

claims.text: ANCHORED only if the dotted prefix is a real module path from the repo root. `daedalus.council.vendors` is; a bare `vendors` resolved through the suffix index is not -- see the note on _suffix_index and the measured false positives below.
claims.why: The code at line 519 sets anchored = _module_file(root, parts[:n], None) is not None, which checks if the prefix resolves without suffix fallback. The comment explains this distinguishes real module paths from suffix-resolved ones.

claims.text: A METHOD documented by its bare name. Prose writes `ollama.py::_run_rewrite` for a method of the class in that file, and pytest's own `file.py::name` addresses a top-level function, so both spellings are in use for the same thing. Measured: the first version of this file called TWO methods missing -- ollama.py::_run_rewrite (line 423) and a test at line 183 -- because it looked only at module scope. Accepting any class member is deliberately LOOSE: it can only turn a finding into a non-finding, which is the direction a checker that dispatches work is allowed to be wrong in.
claims.why: The code at lines 543-549 implements the fallback: if head not in names, it searches classes for head as a member. If found, it returns resolving state. This matches the described behavior.

claims.text: `daedalus.nemesis` against daedalus/__init__.py. The reference names a SUBMODULE that is not in the tree, which is the absent-module case, not the absent-symbol case -- and absent modules are not judged, for the reason the module docstring gives. Measured: the first version of this file reported four of these, and all four were prose that was already correct. `daedalus.nemesis` and `daedalus.cerberus` are log ACTOR names in a namespace convention and `daedalus.root` is a VS Code settings key -- none of the three is a Python attribute at all.
claims.why: The code at lines 551-560 checks if module.name == '__init__.py' and if head not in names (and not found in classes). If so, it returns skipped state with the described reasoning. This matches the claim.

claims.text: Normalise a repo-relative path the way :class:`Reference` records one.
claims.why: The function _rel_key is defined but its behavior is not fully shown; it replaces backslashes with forward slashes. The claim about how Reference records paths cannot be verified without seeing the Reference class.

observations.what: Function _rel_key is defined but incomplete in this chunk; only the docstring and first line are shown.

The fallback to class member lookup uses sorted(classes.items()) which may produce non-deterministic order if class names are not unique; but the code only checks membership, so order does not matter.
The anchored flag is set only for dotted references; path-based references (lines 483-486) set anchored=True unconditionally when candidate is found.
